title: Standing and reciting
hookLine: you stand and recite al-Fatiha, then a short surah
last: TAKBIR — GREATER THAN ALL OF IT.

lines: EYES ON THE PLACE OF PROSTRATION.
cards: The hands come down. In some schools, they fold over the body; in others, they rest at the sides. The eyes drop to the spot where the forehead will touch the ground.
And then, for the first time in the prayer, the person speaks at length. Not a speech. Not a list of requests.
A short chapter you first met in this path's first week, the one that asks for directions. Standing still, in front of no one you can see, saying it as if someone is listening.

teach.h: QIYAM — TO STAND, TO STAND FIRM.
teach.b: The standing is called qiyam, from a root meaning to stand up, to rise, to stand firm.
In it, every unit of the prayer begins with al-Fatiha, the Opening. A hadith in Bukhari is blunt about it: there's no prayer for the one who doesn't recite the Opening of the Book.

So it comes back in every unit of every prayer. It begins, in Pickthall's translation: "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds." And at its center: "Thee (alone) we worship; Thee (alone) we ask for help."
Now the surprise. A hadith qudsi in Sahih Muslim, where the Prophet ﷺ relays words from God, says the prayer is divided between God and the one praying.
When the person says, praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds, God says: My servant has praised Me. At the Beneficent, the Merciful: My servant has extolled Me.

And at the middle line: this is between Me and My servant, and My servant will have what he asks. So in the tradition's own telling, the standing isn't a recital into empty air. It's a conversation, answered line by line.
After the Fatiha, in the first two units, the person adds some other part of the Qur'an, often a short surah from the end of the book, like al-Ikhlas, four lines long.
At dawn, sunset and night, the first two units are recited aloud by the one leading; at midday and afternoon, silently.

how: In each unit of prayer, Muslims stand and recite al-Fatiha in Arabic, adding another passage of the Qur'an in the first two units; at dawn, sunset and night the leader recites the first two units aloud.

games.q: what's inside the standing — tap the pairs.

s: a prayer can be complete without al-Fatiha
a hadith in Bukhari says there's no prayer for one who doesn't recite the Opening of the Book.
a hadith says God answers the Fatiha line by line
a hadith qudsi in Sahih Muslim: My servant has praised Me.
the Fatiha is only recited once in each prayer
it's recited in every unit of every prayer.

games.q: you're standing in prayer and you say, praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds. according to the hadith qudsi, what happens?
o: nothing until the prayer is over
God says: My servant has praised Me
games.why: the hadith qudsi in Muslim says the prayer is divided between God and the servant, and each line is answered.

practice: Stand still, feet a little apart, hands folded or at your sides, eyes resting on a spot on the floor in front of you. If you know the Fatiha, recite it slowly, leaving a small pause after each line, as if waiting for the answer.
If you don't know it, say just its first line in Pickthall's translation, praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds, and stand in the quiet after it.
